Memory.value: Something in my surroundings can instantly bring back the full memory without warning
My memories of the frightening event are very clear and detailed.
Remembering the event brings back the same terror I felt at the time

Negative Appraisals.value: The people or institutions that should have protected me let me down
I feel like I don't know myself anymore
I have permanently changed for the worse

vignette: Margaret, a 70-year-old widowed European woman and former hotel manager, has been struggling with persistent intrusive thoughts since her traumatic encounter with police violence three years ago. The incident occurred during an otherwise uneventful evening at the hotel she managed. A routine call for assistance escalated into a violent confrontation when two officers entered her office, accusing her of harboring illegal activities. Despite her repeated attempts to calm them and assert her innocence, the situation quickly spiraled out of control, leaving Margaret with severe physical injuries and psychological trauma. Since then, Margaret has experienced vivid memories that are triggered without warning by seemingly innocuous events. A loud noise or a sudden movement can instantly transport her back to that harrowing night, reliving every terrifying detail as if it were happening all over again. This unrelenting terror is especially acute on the anniversary of the event, when the trauma feels freshly etched in her mind. Margaret's workplace has become one of her primary triggers due to its crowded nature and constant influx of guests. The mere sight of a group of people can set off a chain reaction of intrusive thoughts, making it increasingly difficult for her to perform her duties with any semblance of normalcy. She found herself canceling shifts or leaving work early on numerous occasions, leading to strained relationships with her colleagues and a significant decline in job performance. In addition to the physical discomfort, Margaret harbors deep-seated negative appraisals about the incident that have profoundly affected her sense of self. She feels that the institutions entrusted to protect her not only failed but actively contributed to her suffering. This belief has eroded her trust and left her feeling vulnerable and uncertain about her future. Moreover, she struggles with a profound loss of identity, unable to reconcile who she was before the event with the person she has become since. Margaret's fear of permanent damage has led her to withdraw from social activities and avoid situations that might trigger her memories. This isolation has strained her relationships and left her feeling disconnected from her community. The cumulative effect of these changes has been a significant deterioration in her quality of life, leaving her yearning for the stability and sense of self she once possessed. What finally brought Margaret to seek help was an acute realization that her current state is unsustainable. She had come to believe that without intervention, her life would continue to spiral downward, and she would never reclaim the sense of security and purpose she once felt. What frightens her most is the prospect of a future defined by fear and uncertainty, but what gives her hope is the possibility of finding a way to live with her memories and regain some semblance of control over her life. In therapy, Margaret hopes to navigate the intricate web of her thoughts and emotions, finding ways to cope with her triggers and rebuild her sense of self. She is eager to explore strategies that might help her re-engage with her community and reclaim aspects of her former identity, ultimately seeking a path towards healing and resilience.
